payload.feature:
The gate-head check is per gate step, never per effect.

Decision 0041 ruling 4: no gate changes the tree, and the engine checks by recording the repository head when a gate effect starts and when it ends, parking GATE-MOVED-HEAD when it moved. The engine keeps that record in one field, `active_gate_head` (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs). A sequence seat arms it at each gate STEP's start (the `step.class == SeatClass::Gate` arm) but only compares and clears it when the whole effect's terminal event is appended (`finish_gate_head_check`, reached from `append` on EffectSucceeded/EffectFailed/EffectIndeterminate). Two consequences:

1. A sequence whose gate step is followed by a work step that commits — lawful under decision 0042 (an author is a work seat) and expressible in any recipe — ends with `start != end` and parks GATE-MOVED-HEAD although the gate never touched the tree. Every shipped sequence happens to end on its gate step, so no shipped recipe trips it today; a recipe author's next sequence will.
2. Any error path that leaves a sequence or single-seat effect without appending a terminal event leaves the field armed for the next effect that appends one.

A first attempt at this (concluded run the-gate-head-check-is-per-gate--8dd5706a, commit 449b491 on the retired branch fire/astra-first) made the check step-local and was judged residual with two medium findings, which this commission folds in as requirements: (1) an all-gate sequence must not ALSO keep an effect-wide arming that a step-local check leaves intact — one observation per gate step and nothing outer; (2) a start or checkpoint failure that propagates out of a gate (single, panel or step) must clear the armed head on the way out, so recovery or an input-digest rejection can never consume a stale observation; the error regression test must exercise the actual error path.

Make the check a property of the gate step: capture the head when a gate step (or a gate single seat) starts, compare and clear it when THAT step ends, and carry a moved head to the effect's terminal event as today so the park reason and its structured evidence are unchanged. A gate step that commits still parks GATE-MOVED-HEAD; a work step that commits after a gate step in the same sequence does not; a gate effect that ends through an error path leaves nothing armed. Keep the frozen event contract untouched (the evidence stays packed in the EffectIndeterminate reason and attached to run/parked).

Prove it in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/tests.rs beside the existing GATE-MOVED-HEAD tests, with fake drivers: (a) a sequence of a read-only gate step then a committing work step completes without a park; (b) a sequence whose gate step commits parks GATE-MOVED-HEAD naming that step's effect; (c) after an effect that errors out of a gate step, the next effect's terminal event runs no stale comparison. Any test that drives a boxed step end-to-end must skip under the in-box marker. `cargo test --workspace` green, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; do not edit contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, reference/ or fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson. No guide explains GATE-MOVED-HEAD today (only decision 0041 does); add one short paragraph to docs/guides/journal-and-verification.md saying what the park means and that the check is per gate step. Update, never remove, existing guide prose.

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Framed in .forge/tasks/gate-head-check-per-gate-step.md: make active_gate_head a property of the gate step (not the whole effect) in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs — remove the effect-wide arm's redundancy under a Sequence body (Defect 1: seat.has_gate can be true for a mixed/all-gate sequence, silently discarding the per-step arm), and clear the field on any Err that propagates out of a gate-armed span before a terminal event is appended (Defect 2: run_driver/run_panel's checkpoint_error path bypasses the terminal-event hook and leaves the field armed for the next effect, as in the digest-mismatch early return at engine.rs:869-889). Pointed the implementer at existing fixtures (compiled_sequence_with_gate, a_compiled_mixed_sequence_guards_the_gate_step_not_the_work_step, fail_event) and specified three new tests (gate-then-committing-work-step completes clean; gate-step-commits still parks naming that step; a checkpoint failure inside a gate leaves no stale comparison for the next effect), plus one guide paragraph in docs/guides/journal-and-verification.md.

The gate-head check is now a property of the gate step. (1) The effect-wide arming in `execute` is asked of the resolved body, not only of the seat: a new `arms_effect_gate_head(body, seat, strategy)` refuses a Sequence outright, so a sequence's per-step arming in `execute_sequence` is the only observation a sequence ever takes — all-gate or mixed, and via Select too, since the check is on the resolved ExecutableBody. (2) The single funnel every body shape passes through (`Cursor::ExecuteEffect => self.execute(...)` in `advance_running`) clears `active_gate_head` when the attempt leaves through an `Err`, so a start or checkpoint failure out of a gate single, panel or sequence step cannot leave an armed head for the next terminal event to spend. The frozen event contract is untouched: evidence stays packed in the EffectIndeterminate reason and copied onto run/parked.

Tests in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/tests.rs: (a) a gate step then a committing work step completes with an EffectSucceeded and no park; (b) a sequence whose gate step commits parks GATE-MOVED-HEAD with head_at_start on the base commit and head_at_end on the gate's own commit, the work step behind it never having run (proved from the tree's commit subjects); (c) a gate single seat whose live checkpoint cannot journal (fail_event on "effect/checkpointed", the real run_driver checkpoint_error path) returns the propagated Err with no terminal event, and the next effect's terminal event carries the in-flight recovery reason with no GATE-MOVED-HEAD anywhere in the journal. Plus a direct test of the arming law: an all-gate sequence seat arms nothing effect-wide, a gate single seat does. The two-step fixture now takes its step order as a parameter instead of gaining a copy. No test drives a boxed step, so no in-box skip was needed.

Verified failing before the fix: (c) parked GATE-MOVED-HEAD on the recovery event with the funnel clear removed; the arming test failed with the old seat-only rule. Defect 1 is an invariant tightening — it is unobservable on today's compiler, since `is_gate_class` reads the sequence branch before a seat's own `class`, so a mixed sequence never compiles to has_gate=true and the outer arm was always overwritten by step 0's; the test therefore pins the law rather than a reproduced park.

Gates: cargo test --workspace green (no failures), cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean, `compile --bundle bundles/self` succeeds. scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself cannot run from this seat (the sandbox refuses `bash <script>` and `awk -f`), so the same report was produced by hand — cargo +nightly llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --locked --branch — and its LCOV tally shows 19468/19468 DA lines covered, zero uncovered/untaken BRDA branches, and 1885/1885 functions covered (0 missed in every file). Guide: one paragraph added to docs/guides/journal-and-verification.md saying what a GATE-MOVED-HEAD park means and that the check is per gate step; no existing prose removed. Nothing under contracts/, policy/, reference/ or fixtures/ was touched. Committed as 015d2da on fire/astra-third, signed; not pushed.
